posts.author: whisky
posts.body:
Being playing RM games since the early 2000's (on rm2k first) and even tough the engine is named
RPG
Maker, why do most people keep making those boring/dull/lame medieval-fantasy non-sense games about "the chosen one hero saving the world"? It's so bad and even worse when they use RTP only/mainly.
We have some amazing project ideas on Rpg Maker but still most games are this same dull thing with that annoying battle system popping-up over the screen all the time. Why? Do something better! Do something new, something fun, do entertaining games.
The saddest thing is all this is that most amazing projects get abandoned by their creator(s)
It's depressing to navigate to the project development boards and already on the titles you get sick of the games!
Do not use stuff like that anymore: "dungeon, dragon, hero, fable, planet/kingdom/town/city, save/saving/savior/salvation, god/angel/devil/demon, fallen, master, order, epic, quest, warrior/samurai", we already had enough of that and it s####.
It's all the same over and over and over again and it's not good, never.
Also, we have a lot of people trying to develop nice games but most great projects get sent into oblivion because they have no support, no help, and no hope that anybody will even care if the project gets made into a full game.
I also suggest that we try to be kinder to the folks posting their projects on game development. Interact, ask, like/dislike, don't let the topics be forgotten with zero posts, it ruins the person's spirit on trying to bring life their ideas for new games. If the game is bad, tell 'em how to improve it; boost the morale.
I believe Rpg Maker has a set of the best and most solid and stable game making engines out there, we can make almost anything in them. Let the dreams come true!

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
I've played terrible sci-fi rpg maker games that don't touch any rpg tropes and incredible fantasy rpg maker games that surround saving a princess. I've also played incredible sci-fi rpg maker games that don't touch any rpg tropes and terrible fantasy rpg maker games that surround saving a princess. It's not the tropes and ideas (or rtp) that make a game fun or not, it's the dev who puts in the effort to make the game they want to make.

posts.author: Arcaines
posts.body:
So certain timelines fit video game genres really well.
Space for all your sci-Fi needs, Medievil for RPGs. Victorian Vampires etc
I get what your saying in some regards to this but it's down to the dev on how they want to make their games. If a certain theme isn't for the players then they simply won't play that game.
I kidna myself do get a little sick on the trope a little, for me it was White Knight Chronicles and this whole "Save the princess's!" thing that I felt was more a cliché then anything else.
As for the Thermology used,  I'll have to disagree with that.
I mean what else you going to name a Samurai? Or a Knight? Reason why people keep to those names because it bring a familiarity to people and gives them a sense of what they do.
